SMTO-FIL-0007 — SMTO couldn't read this file's text format

GUID: b05085a6-9d52-4bf6-9462-1086bab1109e
Slug: file-encoding-error
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • The file's text is stored in a format (its encoding) that SMTO couldn't read, or that doesn't match the one it was told to use, so SMTO stopped instead of garbling it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you know how the file was saved, for example UTF-8, UTF-16 or Latin-1, tell SMTO that encoding in your request. Reading text with the wrong encoding turns letters into errors, so SMTO stops instead.
  2. If you told SMTO to use a specific encoding, remove that instruction and let SMTO detect it. The file may carry its own marker that conflicts with the encoding you named.
  3. If the file uses UTF-32, save it as UTF-8 in a text editor first, or ask SMTO to handle it as raw data. SMTO doesn't support UTF-32 text.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows or edits the file's text with no garbled characters and no error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file's name, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Text decoding or encoding failed: a UnicodeError, a UTF-32 byte-order mark, generic utf-16 requested without a UTF-16 byte-order mark, or a requested codec that conflicts with the file's byte-order mark.

What this means

  • Text conversion raised UnicodeError, encountered unsupported UTF-32, lacked the BOM required for generic UTF-16, or conflicted with the detected BOM/selected codec. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Text conversion raised UnicodeError, encountered unsupported UTF-32, lacked the BOM required for generic UTF-16, or conflicted with the detected BOM/selected codec.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the BOM and intended codec with bounded byte reads; do not repair by silently discarding undecodable data.

How to fix it

  • Detect the file's actual encoding and byte-order mark (for example file -i or a hex dump of the first bytes) and pass the matching encoding (auto, utf-8, utf-8-sig, utf-16, utf-16-le, utf-16-be, latin-1 or cp1252), or use mode=bytes. UTF-32 is unsupported and must be converted or read as bytes.
  • Choose the correct supported encoding or use bytes mode; inspect any BOM conflict.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported explicit encoding matches the file and preserves its intended content.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.
